unit: One fixed graph x pattern-size batch (three graphs x two sizes = six workloads in each suite); each executes its unchanged disjoint development or final query half in five existing interleaved rounds.

metrics.name: exact_counts
metrics.means: Exact equality of every output filename and byte for the complete batch.
metrics.source: SCOPE scope.out local counting results and evaluator._digest_outputs; naive/reference agreement validates the correctness target.
metrics.clears_when: All candidate batch output names and bytes equal the validated reference in every repeated execution.
metrics.tolerance: none; exact hashes with repeated-output stability checks

metrics.name: batch_latency_seconds
metrics.means: Single-core wall seconds of one invocation of the authentic SCOPE batch entrypoint, excluding output hashing and including process execution/cleanup.
metrics.source: SCOPE executable/scope.cpp, existing five rotating interleaved rounds in evaluator._paired_protocol.
metrics.clears_when: Correct counts AND candidate_seconds(w,r) < reference_seconds(w,r) for all five paired rounds r.
metrics.tolerance: No numerical equality allowance. Require five consistent strict timing wins; under independent exchangeable signs the one-sided sign probability is 1/32. No independence or cross-host noise guarantee is asserted.

beats_reference: 1 iff exact_counts AND batch_latency_seconds clear on all six fixed workloads; otherwise 0. All failure paths retain six rows. The original continuous aggregate timing score is separate.

solver_feedback.name: median_seconds
solver_feedback.means: Candidate-only median full-suite elapsed seconds across the five rounds.
solver_feedback.reveals_reference: no — an absolute candidate measurement without reference values, ratios, differences, or private workload labels.

statement_sentences:
The separate `beats_reference` criterion requires both metrics to clear on every workload. A workload is one graph and pattern-size batch: all six fixed combinations are retained in each suite. `exact_counts` requires every output filename and byte to match the validated upstream result. `batch_latency_seconds` requires strictly lower execution time than the paired reference in each of the five existing interleaved rounds on that workload; equality is not a timing win. Correctness is a prerequisite for a timing pass. The continuous score above keeps its original aggregate formula and is independent of this conjunction.

Train feedback includes only your own absolute `median_seconds` for the full suite and `beat_spec_progress` for each metric, with `passed`, `failed`, `total`, `pass_percent`, and `fail_percent`. The denominator is always six workloads. Private workload identities, individual comparison decisions, reference values, speedup ratios, and margins are withheld. Final feedback exposes no metric dictionary.
comments: Supervisor repair of the missing S2 beat-spec contract in the existing collected task. Workloads, source subtraction, reference.patch, timing repetitions, runtime budgets, and continuous scoring remain unchanged. The five-observation consistency rule uses measurements already collected; unlike a fixed percent band it is not extrapolated from unrelated aggregate historical noise. Exact reference patches are already deduplicated by the existing timing protocol and therefore cannot produce a false timing win. Real reference train+final and calibration evidence are recorded separately; no solver result determined this threshold.
